pergunta: What are the top 5 universities in Brazil in 2025 according to the Times Higher Education World University Ranking, and what was the placements of these universities back in 2022?
resposta:
Based on my research, let me compile the information for you. I'll present the top 5 Brazilian universities in the THE World University Rankings 2025 along with their 2022 placements.

---

## Top 5 Universities in Brazil — Times Higher Education World University Rankings

### 🏆 2025 Placements (Global Rank Band)

| # | University | Official Position in THE WUR 2025 | Key Detail |
|---|-----------|----------------------------------|------------|
| **1** | **University of São Paulo (USP)** | **Joint 199th** | First time Brazil entered the top 200 globally; its best performance in over a decade. Driven by improvements in industry income and patents. |
| **2** | **University of Campinas (Unicamp)** | **351–400 band** | Maintained 2nd place in Brazil, moving from the 401–500 band in previous editions. Excels particularly in Teaching (141st globally) and Research Environment (168th). |
| **3** | **Federal University of Rio de Janeiro (UFRJ)** | **601–800 band** | One of Brazil's oldest and most prestigious institutions. Rose into the 601–800 band this year, improving from the 801–1000 band previously. |
| **4** | **Universidade Estadual Paulista (UNESP)** | **601–800 band** | Stayed within the same band as last year. Consistently ranked among Brazil's top 5 public universities. |
| **5** | **Pontifical Catholic University of Rio de Janeiro (PUC-Rio)** | **601–800 band** | Made a notable jump, rising from the 801–1000 band to land in 601–800, becoming Brazil's **joint third-highest ranked institution**. |

> **Note:** The rankings use banded positions for institutions outside the top 200, so exact numerical positions for ranks 3–5 cannot be fully determined—they share the 601–800 band. The order within this band is generally estimated by overall scores and recent movement trends.

---

### 📊 Comparison with 2022 Placement

| University | THE WUR 2025 Position | THE WUR 2022 Position | Change |
|-----------|----------------------|----------------------|--------|
| **USP** | Joint 199th | **201–250 band** | ✅ Significant climb into top 200 |
| **Unicamp** | 351–400 band | **~401–500 band** | ⬆️ Improved by ~50+ positions |
| **UFRJ** | 601–800 band | **~601–800 band** | ➡️ Roughly stable |
| **UNESP** | 601–800 band | **~601–800 or 801–1000 band** | ➡️ Minor movement/likely improvement |
| **PUC-Rio** | 601–800 band | **801–1000 band** | ⬆️ Notable upward shift (~200 positions) |

> In 2022, Brazil had **59 universities** ranked globally, with **USP leading at 201–250** — a full decade later, USP is now joint 199th, marking a major breakthrough for Brazilian higher education internationally.

---

### 💡 Key Observations

- **Brazil finally broke into the global top 200** for the first time ever, thanks mainly to USP's dramatic rise driven by improved industry engagement and patent scores.
- **PUC-Rio's ascent** is particularly notable—it moved up approximately 200 positions between 2022 and 2025.
- **Unicamp has been steadily climbing**, transitioning from the 401–500 range in 2022 to the 351–400 band in 2025, putting it within the top 20% globally for the first time.
- The **THE World University Rankings 2025 included 2,092 universities from 115 countries**, a record expansion, with Brazil adding 5 new institutions since 2024.

**Source links:**
- [THE World University Rankings 2025 Press Release](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/press-releases/times-higher-education-world-university-rankings-2025-released)
- [Shifting Patterns Analysis (THE)](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/world-university-rankings-2025-shifting-patterns)
- [Unicamp's Official Statement on THE 2025 Ranking](https://jornal.unicamp.br/en/noticias/2024/10/09/unicamp-esta-entre-20-das-melhores-universidades-do-mundo-aponta-o-ranking-the/)
- [THE World University Rankings 2022 Press Release](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/press-releases/world-university-rankings-2022-released)

- Oxford holds on to the top spot for the ninth consecutive year, bolstered by significant improvements in industry engagement and teaching

# Top universities in Brazil 2026

![the logo](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/student/dsc/svg/logos/the-logo.svg?1)

## Find the best universities in Brazil using *Times Higher Education*’s Latin America University Rankings 2026. This table has been put together using a trusted methodology that ranks universities on teaching quality, research output and international outlook

#### Share

## Top universities in Brazil 2026

## Key insights into the Brazil University Rankings 2026

- Brazil is among the world’s fastest-growing major economies, with economic reforms that are constantly pushing it forward on the international stage.
- There are 68 universities from Brazil in the [Latin America University Rankings 2026](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/2026/latin-america-university-rankings). It is the most-represented country in the ranking
- Brazilian universities take seven places in the top 10
- The [University of São Paulo](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/university-sao-paulo) is the top-ranked Brazilian university and is also the top institution in the Latin America University Rankings

## Choosing a university in Brazil

Brazil is South America’s fastest-growing economy and this is reflected in the many university options in the bustling cities of Rio de Janeiro and São Paulo, among others. Public university education is free for international and domestic students, so students will most likely only have to pay a registration fee. Private universities do charge fees and this will depend on the course and university.

The table for the best universities in Brazil was derived from data collected from the *THE* Latin America University Rankings. The results are calculated using 18 performance indicators underlying five metrics: research environment, teaching (the learning environment), research quality, industry and international outlook. For more insights and a detailed breakdown of our ranking methodology, [visit our methodology page](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/latin-america-university-rankings-2026-methodology). Use the Brazil university ranking table above to explore the right institution for you.

# University of São Paulo | World University Rankings

The University of São Paulo is a large Brazilian public university, and is considered one of country's more prestigious educational institutions.

Founded in 1934, the University of São Paulo came about through a collaboration of existing schools such as the Faculdade de Direito do Largo de São Francisco (Law), the Polytechnic School (Engineering) and the Escola Superior de Agricultura Luiz de Queiroz (Agriculture).

Now, the university has created new departments, and is one of the largest institutions of higher education in Latin America.

Four of its eleven campuses can be found in the city of São Paulo while the remaining campuses are in the cities of Bauru, Lorena, Piracicaba, Pirassununga, Ribeirão Preto and two in São Carlos.

The university has an remarkable 70 libraries installed across the various campuses for students to use and enjoy.

A significant proportion of scientific papers published by Brazilian researchers are produced at the University of São Paulo.

The university also houses five affiliated hospitals, 24 museums and galleries – with half a million visitors per year – two theatres, a cinema, and its own TV channel run by students.

However, the University of São Paulo have no accommodation within campus, or outside. The search for accommodation must be carried out by students in accordance to their economic conditions and interests.

Notable alumni include Antonio Candido de Mello e Souza, a Brazilian writer, professor, sociologist and literary critic, Brazilian lawyer and Vice President Michel Miguel Elias Temer Lulia, and Guido Mantega, Brazil's former Finance Minister.

# Unicamp is among the 20% of the best universities in the world, according to the THE ranking - News

![The university stood out mainly in the areas of Education and Research Environment, two of the five major pillars analyzed by THE](https://jornal.unicamp.br/wp-content/uploads/sites/32/2024/10/Ju_20241009_-Ranking_THE_Pedro_Amatuzzi_mosaico.jpg)The university stood out mainly in the areas of Education and Research Environment, two of the five major pillars analyzed by THE

Brazil's second-best university, Unicamp, is among the top 20% in the world, according to the *World University Rankings 2025.* Published this Wednesday (9), the ranking is compiled by *Times Higher Education* (THE), one of the pioneering institutions in academic evaluation. For the list, 2092 universities from 115 countries were analyzed. For the first time since the ranking's launch in 2004, Brazil is among the top 20 countries. The University of Oxford (United Kingdom) tops the overall ranking, being considered the best in the world. Among Brazilian universities, the University of São Paulo (USP) took first place.

The *THE World University Rankings 2025* shows Unicamp's evolution in recent years. The University, which appears between 351st and 400th place in the overall ranking, excelled mainly in the areas of Education and Research Environment, two of the five major pillars analyzed by *Times Higher Education* – the others being Research Quality; Industry; and International Outlook. To determine each university's score, 18 performance indicators are considered, distributed across these major areas.

“It is important to highlight that Unicamp has been climbing positions in the rankings, both in the general classification at a global level, moving in the THE from a position between 401 and 500 to one between 351 and 400 in the last two evaluations and maintaining second place at a national level”, said Unicamp rector Antonio José de Almeida Meirelles.

“It is also worth noting that our performance was very good in teaching and in the research environment, with positions closer to the top of the ranking, indicating that we are on the right track in terms of combining these two pillars of the assessment,” he added.

“The Education and Research Environment pillars account for almost 60% of the ranking. In terms of education, Unicamp had a very prominent position in the overall ranking, coming in 141st place. In terms of research environment, it came in 168th place. These indicators maintain the University in a position considered high in relation to the rest of the world”, says Renato Garcia, professor at the University’s Institute of Economics (IE) and advisor to the Pro-Rectory of University Development.

![Advisor to the Pro-Rectorate of University Development, Renato Garcia: position considered high](https://jornal.unicamp.br/wp-content/uploads/sites/32/2024/10/Ju_20241009_-Ranking_THE_scarpa_AJS_2484-Capa.jpg)Advisor to the Pro-Rectorate of University Development, Renato Garcia: position considered high

In terms of industries and patents, Unicamp's performance also stood out, scoring 76,7 points, adds the professor. The university's performance stands out, especially when one takes into account the increase in the number of participants, explains Garcia. Compared to the previous version, 185 new institutions were included in the current ranking. In Brazil alone, there were more than 60 universities.

To produce the 2025 edition of the ranking, THE considered more than 157 million citations in 18 million publications. It also included responses from more than 93 thousand academics from various countries around the world. The teaching environment, volume, revenue and reputation of the research environment are among the points analyzed in the two categories in which Unicamp had its best results.

**Read more:**

[Unicamp is the 3rd best in Latin America for the 2nd consecutive year](https://jornal.unicamp.br/en/noticias/2024/10/03/unicamp-e-3a-na-america-latina-pelo-2o-ano-consecutivo/)

# University of Campinas | World University Rankings

## About the University of Campinas

Basic information and contact details for the University of Campinas

![institution](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/academic-ui-assets/dsc/svg/flat/institution.svg?4)

Campinas is a city in the Sao Paulo state region, and is home to the main campus of the State University of Campinas (Unicamp).

The multi-discipline university also has affiliate campuses in Brazilian cities such as Limeira and Paulínia. Campinas is known not only for its temperate climate at the Tropic of Capricorn but also its wide range of cultural centres such as dozens of cinemas and bars, known locally as “barzinhos”.

The university was opened in 1966, and although one of Brazil’s younger institutions has established itself as a primary medical and scientific research centre. As part of this research and development the university produces a high amount of patented material, outstripping other larger institutions and companies. A major breakthrough was achieved in 2003 when scientists from Unicamp licensed a patent for genetic death detection, and in more recent years scientists at Unicamp have developed a test for detection of the Zika virus.

Also in Campinas and maintaining a strong working relationship with Unicamp is the National Synchrotron Light Laboratory. This institute is a benefit to students studying physics and nanotechnology, and is home to the only particle accelerator in South America. Outside of the sciences, students at Unicamp may take undergraduate courses in arts such as Dance and Communication Studies, or in humanities such as Business Administration and Social Sciences.

International undergraduates will need to sit an exam before acceptance, which will require a strong understanding of the Portuguese language. Like all state run universities, both Brazilian and international students do not pay tuition fees. The most common airport for international students to fly into is the Guarulhos International Airport, located around 135km from the Campinas campus.

Alumni of Unicamp include actor Petrônio Gontijo, historian and gay rights activist Luiz Mott, and economist Paulo Renato Souza.

# THE World University Rankings 2022 Released

**TIMES HIGHER EDUCATION WORLD UNIVERSITY RANKINGS 2022 REVEALS PLANET’S BEST UNIVERSITIES AS UK’S UNIVERSITY OF OXFORD TOPS TABLE FOR 6TH CONSECUTIVE YEAR AND OTHERS SEE BOOST FROM COVID-19 RESEARCH**

- **UK**’s University of Oxford (1st) retains top spot for the sixth consecutive year
- A record 1,662 universities from 99 countries and regions rank, 136 more than last year
- Several universities climb table following success of Covid-19 related research
- **Mainland China** claims highest ever position in table as Tsinghua University and Peking University tie in 16th and sees record number of universities in the top 200 (10)
- **US** (8) and **UK** (2) dominate overall top 10 for the second year in a row
- **Japan**, **South Korea**, **Russia**, **Singapore**, and **Hong Kong** all achieve highest positions since the new methodology was introduced in 2016
- **Hong Kong** records its highest ever number of universities in the top 100 (4)
- Latin America and Caribbean region see record participating universities (125)
- 175 universities make their debuts in the 2022 ranking, **France’s** recent merger university Institut Polytechnique de Paris (95th) is the highest-ranking debutant
- **Palestine** enters rankings for first time in world’s top 500 and is one of five new countries and territories making their debut alongside **Azerbaijan**, **Ecuador**, **Ethiopia** and **Fiji**

- **View the full THE World University Rankings 2022:** <https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/2022/world-ranking>
- **View the full THE World University Rankings 2022 methodology:** <https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/world-university-rankings-2022-methodology>

**2 September 2021**

Times Higher Education (THE) has today announced the results of the THE World University Rankings 2022 with the **UK’s** University of Oxford – which led the way in the global search for a Covid-19 vaccine – retaining top spot for an impressive sixth consecutive year. This is despite a record 1,662 universities from 99 countries and regions appearing in the table. **Azerbaijan**, **Ecuador**, **Ethiopia**, **Fiji** and **Palestine are** all represented for the first time, and include an analysis of 108 million citations to 14.4 million research publications, as well as a survey of over 22,000 academics

**Top Ten Universities Hold On For Fourth Year**

The top 10 positions are all held by the same universities for a second consecutive year, though only three appear in the same ranking position as last year. California Institute of Technology (=2nd), and Harvard University (=2nd) in the **US** both move up, while the **UK**’s University of Cambridge (=5th) climbs back into the top 5 after dropping to 6th last year. Princeton University in the **US** (7th) also improves, moving up two places.

**Below Table: Overall Top 10**

| **University Name** | **Country / Region** | **2022 Rank** | **2021 Rank** | **Change** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| University of Oxford | United Kingdom | 1 | 1 | – |
| California Institute of Technology | United States | =2 | 4 | + 2 |
| Harvard University | United States | =2 | 3 | + 1 |
| Stanford University | United States | 4 | 2 | – 2 |
| University of Cambridge | United Kingdom | =5 | 6 | + 1 |
| Massachusetts Institute of Technology | United States | =5 | 5 | – |
| Princeton University | United States | 7 | 9 | + 2 |
| University of California, Berkeley | United States | 8 | 7 | – 1 |
| Yale University | United States | 9 | 8 | – 1 |
| The University of Chicago | United States | 10 | 10 | – |

**Universities See Boost From Covid-19 Research**

In a year dominated by the ongoing Covid-19 pandemic, the rankings reflect the vital role of universities in understanding and managing the crisis as a number of institutions see significant boosts in their citation scores (which examine university’s research influence, and look at their role in spreading new knowledge and ideas) from Covid-19 focused research.

A number of medical universities moved up the table since last year following Covid-19 research. To name a few, **Mainland China’s** Capital Medical University (501-600), **Taiwan’s** Asia University, Taiwan (501-600), **Saudi Arabia’s** Umm Al-Qura University (601-800), and **Estonia’s** Tallinn University of Technology (601-800), all moved up at least one ranking band as a result.

**Mainland China Continues Rapid Rise**

**Mainland China** enjoys some striking success stories as it continues its rise up the table, with Peking University and Tsinghua University (=16th) claiming **mainland China’s** highest ever finish, and giving it two top 20 places for the first time ever. There are also a record number of **mainland Chinese** universities ranked in the top 200 (10) as Wuhan University (157th), Southern University of Science and Technology (SUSTech) (=162nd), and Huazhong University of Science and Technology (181th) all move into the band.

**The top 200 – Record Highs and New Entrants**

This year, **Japan, South Korea, Russia, Singapore,** and **Hong Kong** all claim their best ever finishes since the current methodology was introduced in 2016 as **Japan’s** University of Tokyo (=35th), **Hong Kong**’s University of Hong Kong (=30th), **South Korea**’s Seoul National University (=54th), **Singapore**’s National University of Singapore (21st), and **Russia**’s Lomonosov Moscow State University (=158th) all climb the table.

The top 200 also sees eight new entrants as universities from mainland China, Germany, Saudi Arabia, Austria, France and Italy all move into the band.

**Below Table: New Entrants into Top 200**

| **University Name** | **Country / Region** | **2022 Rank** | **2021**
**Rank** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Institut Polytechnique de Paris | France | 95 | NA |
| Université Paris-Saclay | France | =117 | NA |
| Wuhan University | Mainland China | 157 | 301–350 |
| Southern University of Science and Technology (SUSTech) | Mainland China | =162 | 251–300 |
| Karlsruhe Institute of Technology | Germany | 180 | 201–250 |
| Huazhong University of Science and Technology | Mainland China | 181 | 301–350 |
| King Abdulaziz University | Saudi Arabia | =190 | 201–250 |
| Medical University of Graz | Austria | 196 | 201–250 |
| University of Hohenheim | Germany | =197 | 201–250 |
| Sapienza University of Rome | Italy | =197 | 201–250 |

**Debutants and Best Represented Countries and Regions**

**France’s** Institut Polytechnique de Paris (95th) is the highest ranked of 175 debutant universities this year (following its recent merger), and the only one to rank in the top 100, closely followed by another **French** university (and recent merger, formerly 'University Paris-Saclay’), Université Paris-Saclay (=117th). No other university debuts in the top 200.

The highest number of new entrants are from the **US** (14), helping it achieve a record number of ranked institutions as a result (183). Following close behind are **Iran** and **Russia** both with 12 new entrants, **Turkey** (11), **Brazil** and **India** (both 9).

**Below Table: Total and highest ranked debutant universities by country**

- **Country / Region** **Total Debutants** **Top Ranked Debutant** **2022 Rank**
- United States 14 University of South Florida 201-250
- Iran 12 Mazandaran University of Medical Sciences 351-400
- Russia 12 Plekhanov Russian University of Economics 501-600
- Don State Technical University 501-600
- Turkey 11 Istanbul University-Cerrahpaşa 801-1000
- Istanbul Medeniyet University 801-1000
- Brazil 9 Federal Rural University of Pernambuco 1201+
- Federal University of Tocantins 1201+
- Federal University of Vales do Jequitinhonha e Mucuri 1201+
- Mackenzie Presbyterian University 1201+
- Universidade Federal da Grande Dourados 1201+
- Universidade Federal do Triângulo Mineiro 1201+
- Universidade Nove de Julho (Uninove) 1201+
- University of Passo Fundo (UPF) 1201+
- University of Pernambuco 1201+
- India 9 JSS Academy of Higher Education and Research 351-400
- France 8 Institut Polytechnique de Paris 95th
- Mainland China 8 Guangzhou University 601-800

Once again, the **US** is the most represented country or region in the ranking (183 universities). They are followed by **Japan** (118), **UK** (101), **mainland China** (97), and India (71). **Fiji**, **Azerbaijan**, **Ecuador**, **Ethiopia**, and **Palestine** are all represented for the first time. Except Ecuador (six), these debut countries and regions see one unversity appear in the table.

**Below Table: Top represented countries and territories in the THE World University Rankings 2022**

| **Country / Region** | **Total Ranked Universities** | **Top performing university** | **2022 Rank** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| United States | 183 | California Institute of Technology;
Harvard University | =2 |
| Japan | 118 | The University of Tokyo | =35 |
| United Kingdom | 101 | University of Oxford | 1 |
| China | 97 | Peking University;
Tsinghua University | =16 |
| India | 71 | Indian Institute of Science | 301–350 |
| Russian Federation | 60 | Lomonosov Moscow State University | =158 |
| Brazil | 59 | University of São Paulo | 201–250 |
| Iran | 58 | Kurdistan University of Medical Sciences;
Babol Noshirvani University of Technology; Mazandaran University of Medical Sciences | 351–400 |
| Turkey | 54 | Cankaya University | 401–500 |
| Spain | 52 | Pompeu Fabra University | 156 |

**Phil Baty, Chief Knowledge Officer, THE, commented:**

“*The world’s elite universities have enjoyed a long period of dominance at the top of the table with help from historic repuatation, global status, and reliable income. But our data shows us that there are clear shifts happening across higher education around the world. We are already seeing clear disruption to the established norms from mainland China, and record highs for Japan, South Korea, Singapore, and Hong Kong show that Asia is continuing to benefit from the focus and investment in higher education across the continent.*

*In the coming years it will be interesting to see whether the US, UK and other world-leading higher education systems can respond to the challenges of Covid-19, including attracting international academic and student talent, and a possibly serious impact on already stretched funding, to hold onto their positions at the very top of the table.”*

# Times Higher Education World University Rankings 2025 released

- Oxford overtakes California Institute of Technology and Harvard’s records in the number one spot as Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) has become the highest-ranked US university for the first time overtaking Stanford University.
- The reputation of UK and US universities have both significantly declined this year.
- The number of countries in the top 200 increased by three to 30 this year. They are: Brazil, Saudi Arabia and United Arab Emirates.
- Seven countries are ranked for the first time: Bahrain, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Mongolia, Paraguay, Rwanda, Syria and Uzbekistan.
- The 21st year of the ranking has a record 2,092 universities ranked – up from 1,907 last year – from 115 countries and regions.
- The US has the most institutions ranked with 174, followed by Japan with 119, and joint third are UK and India with 107 each.

**Oxford University enjoys record-breaking year at the top, but US and UK sectors face drops in reputation**

The University of Oxford takes the top spot for a record-breaking ninth consecutive year in the*Times Higher Education* (*THE*) World University Rankings 2025, released today. Oxford has beaten Harvard University’s previous record of eight consecutive years at the number one spot from 2004 to 2011.

However, the reputation of the UK higher education sector is increasingly fragile as its top universities have declined for the second year in a row as the sector faces a severe financial crisis. The UK recorded the worst year-on-year decline in research reputation among large countries (with at least 50 ranked institutions). UK universities received 19 per cent of votes (for teaching and research combined) in the survey in 2016, compared with 15 per cent today.

US universities dominate the top 10 taking seven spots. Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) is now the highest-ranked US university in second place, its best-ever performance, while Stanford University dropped from second to sixth. The country has 23 universities in the top 50, 38 in the top 100 and 55 in the top 200 – more than any other country.

But the global reputation of US universities is at a record low. American universities received 47 per cent of the votes (for teaching and research combined) in *THE*’s 2016 reputation survey and this dropped sharply to 38 per cent this year - the steepest long-term decline of any country.

***THE*****’s top 10 universities in the world**

| **University** | **Country** | **Rank 2025** | **Rank 2024** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| University of Oxford | United Kingdom | 1 | 1 |
| Massachusetts Institute of Technology | United States | 2 | 3 |
| Harvard University | United States | 3 | 4 |
| Princeton University | United States | 4 | 6 |
| University of Cambridge | United Kingdom | 5 | 5 |
| Stanford University | United States | 6 | 2 |
| California Institute of Technology | United States | 7 | 7 |
| University of California, Berkeley | United States | 8 | 9 |
| Imperial College London | United Kingdom | 9 | 8 |
| Yale University | United States | 10 | 10 |

After two years of decreasing participation, the number of **Chinese mainland** universities surged back up to 94 this year and of those 26 improved on last year’s positions and six fell – a net change of +20; an improvement rate of 21 per cent. **Chinese mainland** had the second-highest improvement rate of all countries in the ranking, coming behind only **Sweden**, which saw seven universities improve and three drop down – an improvement rate of 31 per cent.

In 2021, the **US** had 59 universities in the top 200; this has now dropped to 55. The **UK**’s top 200 has also decreased since 2021, from 29 to 25, and Germany’s from 21 to 20. **Chinese mainland** and **Japan** are the only countries to increase their representation in the top 200 by more than one during this time, by six and three respectively. Chinese mainland now has 13 and Japan has five.

While the **UK**’s total has remained largely stable since 2021, the number of **Indian** institutions has risen rapidly in the past two years – jumping up to 107 in the 2025 edition from 75 in the 2023 edition. **Turkey** has also experienced fast growth, increasing from 43 in the 2021 edition to 91 in the 2025 edition.

Over the past five years, **Asia** has contributed the most new entrants to the ranking. Of the 211 universities that joined the ranking for the first time since the 2021 edition, 60 per cent are from **Asia**, 17 per cent from **Europe**, 10 per cent from **Africa**, and 10 per cent from **South America**.

**Egypt** saw the highest increase in the number of universities, adding seven new institutions since last year. **Nigeria** followed with an increase of six universities. In Europe, **France** experienced the largest growth with six additional universities. In South America, both **Brazil** and **Argentina** added five universities each.

Arab countries are doing exceptionally well with universities from **Saudi Arabia** and the **United Arab Emirates** entering the top 200. **Sub-Saharan Africa** has seen participation increase by 26 per cent year-on-year with ranked universities increasing from 42 last year to 53 this year. The highest-ranked university in **Africa** is University of Cape Town in joint 180th.

The **Latin America region** sees a university enter the top 200 this year with **Brazilian** institution University of São Paulo at joint 199th – its best performance for more than a decade. A record 166 universities from 13 countries are ranked from the region.

The 21st edition of the ranking has 2,092 universities ranked – up from 1,907 last year – from 115 countries and regions. This marks an increase of 9.7 per cent since last year, making it the biggest rise in the past five years and comparing to a 6 per cent growth last year.

The *THE* **World University Rankings 2025** are the most comprehensive, rigorous and balanced global ranking assessing research-intensive universities across 18 performance indicators, which are divided into five pillars, covering their core missions of teaching, research, knowledge transfer and internationalisation.

**Phil Baty, Times Higher Education’s chief global affairs officer, said**: “Oxford University’s achievement of being ranked first in the world for a record nine years, in a row, in *Times Higher Education*’s World University Rankings, is just an unbelievably phenomenal achievement.

“It is all the more impressive given the ever-increasing competition in our ranking as more and more universities participate each year with more than 2,000 assessed this year.

“I want to make a special point of congratulating every ranked university - simply being included in the ranking is something to celebrate as we focus on a couple of thousand global research universities among the tens of thousands of higher education institutions worldwide.

“*Times Higher Education’s* World University Rankings is the world’s gold-standard for ranking research-intensive universities. It’s unparalleled in participation, rigour and is the most trusted and respected ranking of its kind – where we have taken 21 years to carefully build up its reputation and prestige.”

This year 2,860 institutions submitted data, up six per cent on last year (last year it was 2,674) from 133 countries and territories. The World University Rankings 2025 has 2,092 ranked universities meaning 768 institutions gained “reporter” status, which means, although they submitted data, they did not meet *THE*’s eligibility criteria to receive a ranking.

The *THE* World University Rankings started with 200 universities and now has more than 2,000 making it the most global and inclusive ranking in the world.

***View the full [World University Rankings 2025 results](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/2025/world-ranking) and see [World University Rankings 2025 methodology](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/world-university-rankings-2025-methodology).***

# Federal University of Rio de Janeiro | World University Rankings

The Federal University of Rio de Janeiro, sometimes known as the "University of Brazil" and commonly abbreviated to UFRJ, is one of the largest and best known universities in Brazil. Founded by the Brazilian State in 1792, the university has gone on to have an enormous influence on public life in Rio, being responsible for laboratories, libraries and hospitals.

The University operates across a number of campuses and facilities throughout Rio de Janeiro, but is primarily focused on Ilha do Fundão, an artificial island off the western shore of Rio’s famous Guanabara Bay. This campus, known as College City, offers a huge range of services and activities for students including a free shuttle bus services for crossing Rio de Janeiro, various restaurants and cafes, a sports centre, as well as accommodation for students.

UFRJ can also lay claim to a number of high-quality academic facilities, such as the largest ocean tank in the world, as well as a domestically operated maglev train system.

As one might expect for a higher education institution of this size and reach, UFRJ offers a huge range and variety of undergraduate courses (more than 170), as well and numerous avenues for postgraduate and research students. UFRJ also distinguishes itself with a significant level of international co-operation, with extensive opportunities for foreign students to come and study in Rio.

The university can also boast of having produced a succession of successful alumni, including writer Jorge Amado, Nobel Peace Prize nominee Osvaldo Aranha, and physician Oswaldo Cruz.

# Rankings of universities in Brazil

For broader coverage of this topic, see [Universities and Higher Education in Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universities_and_Higher_Education_in_Brazil "Universities and Higher Education in Brazil").

Universities in [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil "Brazil") are ranked in a number of ways, including both national and international ranks.

## National Rankings

### Ranking Universitário Folha

Paulo") has organized a national ranking of universities[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rankings_of_universities_in_Brazil#cite_note-RUF-1) with criteria akin to those used by better known worldwide rankings: research, teaching, internationalization, innovation and market value.

### Brazilian government evaluation

Higher education evaluations are also conducted by the Brazilian Government; specifically by **Inep** (Instituto Nacional de Estudos e
Pesquisas Educacionais; English: National Institute of Studies and Research). The Government uses a **General Index of Courses** (Portuguese: [Índice Geral de Cursos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Índice_Geral_de_Cursos?action=edit&redlink=1 "Índice Geral de Cursos (page does not exist)") [[pt](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Índice%20Geral%20de%20Cursos "pt:Índice Geral de Cursos")]; **IGC**) to determine the quality of Brazilian's higher education (graduate and post-graduate courses) in [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil "Brazil"). [Universidade de São Paulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universidade_de_São_Paulo "Universidade de São Paulo"), one of the most prestigious universities in the country, has been participating in the **IGC** since 2013 as part of a technical cooperation with **Inep** that will last three years, during which time the results concerning the university's courses will not be disclosed. Only then will the university decide whether to fully participate in the government evaluation.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rankings_of_universities_in_Brazil#cite_note-RUF-1)

# World University Rankings 2025: Top universities go global

- The World University Rankings used to be dominated by the UK and the US.

- The World University Rankings 2025 are much more international.

- The Global South now plays a much bigger role.

When the World University Rankings first emerged 20 years ago, they were very much a UK initiative. The creation of the global league table was first recommended in a 2003 report to the UK government by Richard Lambert, a former director general of the Confederation of British Industry and a one-time chairman of the British Museum.

His *Lambert Review* on university-business collaboration explained that “a league table of the world’s best research-intensive universities would provide the government with a way of assessing its research funding efforts,” in a context in which “government policy is to finance university research in such a way as to ensure that the UK has a number of institutions able to compete with the best in the world.”

Eleven months after the *Lambert Review*, in November 2004, the UK-based [Times Higher Education](http://www.timeshighereducation.com/) (THE) published the first edition of the *THE World University Rankings*. The assurance Lambert sought for the UK government was provided: the UK had two of the world’s top ten universities in that first edition, Oxford and Cambridge; and, 30 of the full list of 200 universities. That’s 15% of all ranked universities. The US occupied 31%, with 62 of the 200, including seven of the top ten and all four of the top spots, with Harvard in first place.

## UK and US still dominate the top ten

Today, twenty years on, while the very top of the list remains remarkably similar to that of 2004, and the UK and US still dominate the highest ranks, the [*2025 edition of the THE World University Rankings*](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/latest/world-ranking) represents a very different and more dynamic global university sector – and much more competitive geopolitics of knowledge and innovation.

![](https://assets.weforum.org/editor/n_seq-Y0hm18WhFJqvBY4fKqZnyrre66bA3Bsg0g_Js.jpg?w=1024)

Image: Times Higher Education

[The rankings](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/world-university-rankings-2025-key-trends) show a thriving, diverse global research community, with many more universities across the world publishing world-class research, a much more even distribution of excellence across the continents and a global levelling up of excellence between the dominant West and the rising East – as well as the steady rise of the Global South.

The ranking has grown from 200 universities in 2004 to over 2,000 in 2025. The US makes up 8% of all ranked institutions (down from 31% in 2004) while the UK takes 5% (down from 15%). The 2025 edition includes 115 countries, compared to 29 countries in 2004. India now matches the UK’s total tally of ranked universities, with 107, while China takes 94 places and Hong Kong six. Pakistan has 47 places.

## Africa moves up the rankings

Africa’s representation is surging, as more institutions develop their research infrastructure, increase research productivity and seek to compete with the best in the world. Nigeria added six universities to the global rankings, taking its total to 21, while in the north, Egypt added seven to reach 35.

Seven countries make their debuts in the world rankings: Bahrain; Democratic Republic of the Congo; Mongolia; Paraguay; Rwanda; Syria and Uzbekistan, as their universities begin to compete in global research.

And, the two decades since the first ranking have not just witnessed the emergence of a much more diverse range of countries with universities represented among the growing global research elite – it has also seen a surge in performances that challenge the traditionally dominant Western nations.

The composition of the 2025 top 200 is revealing.

![](https://assets.weforum.org/editor/4EE4KD_gtlUkLCtuytcS2JcQ9JBkMup0GhJ2O6uT9ss.jpg?w=1024)

Image: Times Higher Education

For 2025, the US has 55 of the top 200 group, down from 62 in 2004. The UK has 25, down from 30.

In the immediate term, other Western powerhouses are under pressure. In the Netherlands, of its 11 top-200 universities, seven have fallen in the rankings for 2025 and the country – facing major research funding cuts and a clamp down on internationalization – has lost its top 50 status as Delft University of Technology slips from 48th to 56th. Australia now has just ten universities in the world's top 200, down from 12 as recently as 2021 – and eight of the remaining ten have fallen this year.

![This professor asked ChatGPT to design a university course. Here's what happened](https://cdn.jwplayer.com/thumbs/BIStL9k0-1280.jpg)

This professor asked ChatGPT to design a university course. Here's what happened

03:55

## The Far East increases its representation

In contrast, the Far East is thriving. China has 13 of the top 200, compared to two for most of the 2000s and Hong Kong has seen its representation rise from four to six.

China’s Beijing powerhouse universities, Tsinghua University and Peking University this year occupy record high positions of 12th and 13th in the world respectively, edging ever closer to the elite global top 10. Hong Kong’s universities are rising to consolidate positions in the top 100, with the Chinese University of Hong Kong entering the top 50 (44th from 53rd) closing in on Hong Kong University, which holds firm in 35th place.

Singapore’s two global research universities, for the first time ever, now occupy world top-30 positions – with National University of Singapore rising to 17th from 19th last year and Nanyang Technological University, one of the fastest-rising universities in the world over the last decade, moving from 32nd to 30th. South Korea now has six top 200 universities, compared to three in 2004.

## Upward movement in the Middle East, too

Moreover, the 2025 edition has seen some eye-catching top-200 breakthroughs. In the Middle East, Saudi Arabia has a debuting world top-200 university with King Fahd University of Petroleum and Minerals taking 176th place and other Saudi universities surging up the rankings. The United Arab Emirates has its first top 200 place, with Abu Dhabi University taking 191st and all of its top five universities rose.

In South America, Brazil has broken into the top 200, with the University of Sao Paulo taking 199th place.

# Top universities in Brazil 2026

![the logo](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/student/dsc/svg/logos/the-logo.svg?1)

## Find the best universities in Brazil using *Times Higher Education*’s Latin America University Rankings 2026. This table has been put together using a trusted methodology that ranks universities on teaching quality, research output and international outlook

#### Share

## Top universities in Brazil 2026

## Key insights into the Brazil University Rankings 2026

- Brazil is among the world’s fastest-growing major economies, with economic reforms that are constantly pushing it forward on the international stage.
- There are 68 universities from Brazil in the [Latin America University Rankings 2026](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/2026/latin-america-university-rankings). It is the most-represented country in the ranking
- Brazilian universities take seven places in the top 10
- The [University of São Paulo](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/university-sao-paulo) is the top-ranked Brazilian university and is also the top institution in the Latin America University Rankings

## Choosing a university in Brazil

Brazil is South America’s fastest-growing economy and this is reflected in the many university options in the bustling cities of Rio de Janeiro and São Paulo, among others. Public university education is free for international and domestic students, so students will most likely only have to pay a registration fee. Private universities do charge fees and this will depend on the course and university.

The table for the best universities in Brazil was derived from data collected from the *THE* Latin America University Rankings. The results are calculated using 18 performance indicators underlying five metrics: research environment, teaching (the learning environment), research quality, industry and international outlook. For more insights and a detailed breakdown of our ranking methodology, [visit our methodology page](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/latin-america-university-rankings-2026-methodology). Use the Brazil university ranking table above to explore the right institution for you.

# World University Rankings 2025: shifting patterns

### [**Browse the latest results of the World University Rankings**](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/latest/world-ranking)

If the World University Rankings were a person it would now be allowed to drink in the US. In this 21st edition we are raising a glass to the biggest table yet, with more than 2,000 institutions ranked and 115 countries represented for the first time. Cheers!

This year sees some interesting trends, including the [University of Oxford](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/university-oxford) reigning supreme with the [longest run in the top spot ever](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/news/world-university-rankings-2025-results-announced), though a [drop in reputation for UK universities](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/talking-leadership/oxford-v-c-fears-impact-declining-uk-sector-reputation) on the whole.

Elsewhere, it’s all change for elite US universities, which are switching positions; [Australia appears to be losing ground](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/news/world-university-rankings-2025-australia-stands-precipice); the Netherlands could be one to watch; and we have a more diverse top 200.

There are also seven countries that are ranked for the first time this year: Bahrain, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Mongolia, Paraguay, Rwanda, Syria and Uzbekistan.

---

**Oxford and the UK**

The University of Oxford has retained its number one spot for the ninth year in a row, making it the longest reign in the history of the rankings (the [California Institute of Technology](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/california-institute-technology) was previously top for five years and, before that, Harvard led for eight).

Oxford’s industry score (based on industry income and, since last year, patents) has significantly increased in recent years, as has its teaching environment score. But when comparing its performance against other institutions in the top five, it stands out for its international outlook (particularly proportion of international students and international co-authorship).

The UK sector has less positive news, however, when it comes to reputation. Among the 12 British universities in the global top 100, the average teaching and research reputation scores have dropped for the second year in a row.

![World University Rankings graph showing reputation score of UK universities in the global top 100, 2016-2024](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/sites/default/files/styles/article785xauto/public/reputation-of-uk-universities.jpg?itok=k1dAdqEu "World University Rankings graph showing reputation score of UK universities in the global top 100, 2016-2024")

Among large countries – the 11 nations with at least 50 institutions ranked this year and last year – the UK recorded the worst year-on-year decline in research reputation.

Victor Melatti, data scientist at *Times Higher Education*, says that part of the reason for the UK’s drop is that the reputation survey has expanded in recent years, with scholars from more countries participating, leading to a broader distribution of votes.

The survey received votes from more than 93,000 academics in the past two years combined, up from about 22,000 in 2019 and 2020. UK universities received 19 per cent of votes (for teaching and research combined) in the survey in 2016, compared with 15 per cent today; the US has seen an even steeper long-term decline, from 47 per cent to 32 per cent.

![World University Rankings graph showing research reputation vote share, 2015-2024](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/sites/default/files/styles/article785xauto/public/reserarch-reputation-vote-share.jpg?itok=UsUB9EIg "World University Rankings graph showing research reputation vote share, 2015-2024")

However, the more significant year-on-year drop for the UK in research reputation, compared with the US, suggests there might be other factors at play too. And this decline may worsen in future years given that UK universities are facing a funding crisis, with [one in three making redundancies](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/news/too-hard-too-fast-one-three-campuses-now-making-redundancies) in a climate of high inflation, frozen English tuition fees and [declining international enrolments](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/news/uk-international-postgraduate-recruitment-slumps-44-cent#:~:text=UK%20overseas%20postgraduate%20recruitment%20).

**US movement at the top**

US universities continue to dominate the top 10, but there have been shifts in their positions. [Stanford University](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/stanford-university) has dropped from second to sixth, its lowest position since 2010, driven by a fall in its score for teaching from 99.0 to 97.5 and slightly lower scores for research environment and international outlook. Digging deeper, the drop under teaching is due to a lower score for doctorate-to-staff ratio; it has also declined when it comes to research income and productivity, and international staff and co-authorship.

The [Massachusetts Institute of Technology](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/massachusetts-institute-technology) (MIT) – now the highest-ranked US university at second place, its best-ever performance – [Harvard University](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/harvard-university), [Princeton University](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/princeton-university) and the [University of California, Berkeley](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/university-california-berkeley) have all moved up the ranking.

MIT and Princeton are proving to be dark horses, with the data revealing steady improvements in their positions since 2016. Princeton appears to have improved where Stanford declined: with better scores under doctorate-to-staff ratio as well as doctorate-to-bachelor ratio. It has also improved in terms of industry income, with a score of 93.7 this year, up from 90.2 last year. Meanwhile, MIT has progressed in all metrics over the past 10 years.

Overall, the US has slightly improved its representation in the top league, with 38 institutions ranked in the top 100, up from 36 last year. However, there appears to be a hollowing out of the next tier – those ranked between 101 and 200. There are now only 17 US universities in this group, its lowest number ever. These institutions have suffered drops in teaching reputation, research productivity and three metrics relating to research quality.

![World University Rankings graph showing number of US institutions ranked in 101-200 band, 2016-2025](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/sites/default/files/styles/article785xauto/public/us-institutions-ranked-101-200.jpg?itok=IAIk3yzk "World University Rankings graph showing number of US institutions ranked in 101-200 band, 2016-2025")

Among large countries – the 11 nations with at least 50 institutions ranked this year and last year – the US recorded the third worst year-on-year decline in average research quality score.

#### **A more diverse top 200**

For the past four years, the number of countries represented in the top 200 has remained steady at 27, but this year it has risen to 30.

One of the new countries is the United Arab Emirates, represented by [Abu Dhabi University](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/abu-dhabi-university), the first institution in the country to reach the top 200. It is ranked joint 191st, up from the 251-300 band last year. The university has higher scores in the teaching environment, research environment and research quality pillars.

![World University Rankings graphs showing average change in research reputation and research quality scores for countries with 50 or more ranked universities](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/sites/default/files/styles/article785xauto/public/change-in-research-scores.jpg?itok=plglJLFs "World University Rankings graphs showing average change in research reputation and research quality scores for countries with 50 or more ranked universities")

In 2021, the US had 59 universities in the top 200; this has now dropped to 55. The UK’s count has also decreased, from 29 to 25, and Germany’s from 21 to 20. China and Japan are the only countries to increase their representation in the top 200 by more than one during this period, by six and three respectively. China now has 13 and Japan has five.

The [University of São Paulo](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/university-sao-paulo) in Brazil has also just cracked the top 200 at joint 199th, the institution’s best performance since 2013. The main factor behind its rise is its improvement in industry (income and patents).

[Pontifical Catholic University of Rio de Janeiro (PUC-Rio)](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/pontifical-catholic-university-rio-de-janeiro-puc-rio), the country’s joint third-highest ranked institution, also improved its position, rising from band 801-1,000 to 601-800 this year. The three others in Brazil’s top five have stayed in the same bands. Brazil now has 61 universities ranked, with five institutions added this year. Compared with the rest of South America, Brazilian universities have the highest average score in the teaching, research environment and industry pillars.

This could represent a turning point for the country’s higher education system. While it continues to suffer from years of underfunding, the ousting of anti-intellectual Jair Bolsonaro as president nearly two years ago might be starting to have an impact.

#### **Decline in Oceania**

For the second year in a row, Australia’s elite universities have slipped down the rankings; the top five are all ranked lower than they were last year. The [University of Melbourne](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/university-melbourne), the country’s highest-ranked institution, has dropped from 37th to 39th; [Monash University](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/monash-university) from 54th to joint 58th; the University of Sydney from 60th to 61st; [Australian National University](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/australian-national-university) from 67th to joint 73rd; and the University of Queensland from 70th to 77th.

In 2021, Australia had 12 universities in the top 200, but it now has 10.

Looking at the average pillar scores of Australia’s top 10 universities, we can see that the drops are driven by reductions in the teaching and research environment pillars. The average teaching score for these institutions is 46.9, compared with 48.2 last year, and the average for research environment is 57.4, compared with 59.0 last year.

Of Australia’s total 38 universities ranked, four have gone up, 17 down, 16 remain unchanged and one was not ranked last year.

Experts point to the loss of international student revenue, due to border closures during the pandemic and some of the world’s longest lockdowns, as a key reason for the decline.

However, Merlin Crossley, deputy vice-chancellor at the University of New South Wales (UNSW) Sydney, is confident that the country’s performance will recover.

“In the last 15 years, Australian universities have shone on the world stage. Our top institutions have bounced back after Covid and the rapid return of international students is temporarily throwing out some of the ratios and reducing our scores, though the actual quality in our system has been sustained,” he says. “I’m optimistic that the momentum to invest in staff and research will continue in Australia and we’ll keep up with our impressive Asian neighbours.”

Neighbouring New Zealand is also struggling. The [University of Auckland](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/university-auckland), the country’s top performer, has dropped from joint 150th to joint 152nd. Of New Zealand’s eight universities in the ranking, three have declined and five have retained their positions.

#### **All change in the Netherlands**

In the Netherlands, eight of the 12 institutions ranked have dropped down the table, but the other four have risen.

The country’s highest performer, [Delft University of Technology](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/delft-university-technology), has slipped out of the top 50, dropping from 48th to joint 56th. Conversely, the country’s second-highest performer, the [University of Amsterdam](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/university-amsterdam), has risen from 61st to joint 58th. [Erasmus University Rotterdam](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/erasmus-university-rotterdam) has dropped out of the top 100, from joint 99th last year to joint 107th.

The change for Delft University of Technology was driven by a reduced score for teaching. Its score for international outlook has improved, but the Netherlands could be a country to watch when it comes to global links. The new coalition government, with the far-right Party for Freedom now the largest party, has proposed restrictions on international students and researchers, including [limitations on English-language instruction](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/news/dutch-universities-cut-english-only-undergraduate-degrees) and higher tuition fees for students from outside the European Union.

tool_trace.content:
# As Universidades brasileiras nos rankings mundiais

- 1 Théry, H. (2010). Classificações de universidades mundiais, "Xangai" e outras . Estudos Avançados, [(...)](https://journals.openedition.org/confins/58999#ftn1)

1Um artigo publicado na revista *Estudos avançados**[1](https://journals.openedition.org/confins/58999#ftn1)* tinha analisado *o Academic Ranking of World Universities (Arwu),* conhecido como “ranking de Xangai”, examinando mais de perto seu funcionamento e plotando seus dados em um mapa-múndi para mostrar a geografia do que ele considera “as principais universidades do mundo”. Como outros rankings foram elaborados em resposta às deficiências e vieses dele, três deles também tinham analisados e mapeados.

2A edição de 2024 do Arwu, publicada em 15 de agosto de 204, oferece uma ocasião para fazer um balanço da sua evolução, mais uma vez mapeando seus resultados e comparando-os com os de outros rankings, e depois situar as universidades brasileiras nesse contexto global.

3O primeiro mapa mostra as 100, 500 e 1.000 melhores universidades por país, de acordo com essa classificação. O segundo compara a posição das universidades brasileiras nos rankings Arwu 2024 e 2008 (que foi usado no artigo anterior) e em dois outros rankings para 2024, o do *Center for World University Ranking* (CWUR) e o do *Times Higher Education*. Como os resultados desse último são bastante diferentes daqueles do Arwu (devido aos critérios em que se baseia), um terceiro mapa traça uma tipologia que esclarece os resultados diferenciados das universidades brasileiras.

## [O contexto global](https://journals.openedition.org/confins/58999#tocfrom1n1)

4O ranking Arwu compara instituições de ensino superior. Em 2024 ele classificou 1.000 instituições, levando em conta seis indicadores, principalmente relacionados à pesquisa: o número de ganhadores do Prêmio Nobel e da Medalha Fields entre seus ex-alunos e professores, o número de citações de pesquisadores, o número de artigos publicados nas revistas *Science* e *Nature*, o número de artigos no *Science Citation Index* e no *Social Sciences Citation Index*.

5Em termos de número de universidades por milhão de habitantes, o “Ocidente” (América do Norte, Europa, Austrália) continua dominando, com os Estados Unidos na liderança entre as 100 e 500 melhores. Mas a China é agora o país com o maior número de universidades entre as 1.000 melhores da lista, e outros países asiáticos estão seguindo o seu exemplo: a Coreia do Sul sobe 7 posições e o Japão 2, quando se passa das 500 para as 1.000 melhores.

6Usando o mesmo cálculo, o sul da Europa sobe (Itália e Espanha ganham 15 posições) e o norte da Europa desce (Bélgica cai 2 posições, Holanda e Suécia 3, França 4). A queda no número de países menores entre os 1.000 primeiros é, sem dúvida, parcialmente devida a um efeito de tamanho: a Suíça cai 15 posições, a Dinamarca 17, Israel 18, enquanto o Brasil sobe 10 posições.

Figura 1 Ranking Arwu 2024, das 100, 5000 e 1000 melhores universidades por país

[![Figura 1 Ranking Arwu 2024, das 100, 5000 e 1000 melhores universidades por país](https://journals.openedition.org/confins/docannexe/image/58999/img-1-small480.jpg)](https://journals.openedition.org/confins/docannexe/image/58999/img-1-small580.jpg)

## [Situação das universidades brasileiras](https://journals.openedition.org/confins/58999#tocfrom1n2)

7Existem outros rankings além do Arwu, em 2010, dois tinham sido analisados: o da *École des Mines de Paris*, baseado no número de ex-alunos entre os diretores das 500 maiores empresas do mundo, e o do laboratório *Cybermetrics*, que analisava a qualidade da informação nos sites das universidades. Nenhum deles é mais produzido, e foi necessário procurar outros.

- Entre eles está o da *QS University ranking* publicado desde 2011 por Quacquarelli Symonds, após seu rompimento com o *The Times* (veja abaixo) e a classificação de Leiden. Nenhum deles foi satisfatório, o primeiro porque era muito redundante com o Arwu, o segundo porque baseado exclusivamente em indicadores bibliométricos). Dois outros foram escolhidos

-   - 2 Desde 2016, sua sede está localizada nos Emirados Árabes Unidos.

    O jornal britânico *The Times* tem publicado o *THE World University Rankings* desde 2004 em sua publicação mensal *Times Higher Education*. O *Center for World University Rankings (CWUR)*, criado em 2012 em Jeddah, na Arábia Saudita[2](https://journals.openedition.org/confins/58999#ftn2), avalia a qualidade da educação, empregabilidade, corpo docente e pesquisa. Em 2019, as suas classificações foram ampliadas, com 20.966 instituições classificadas e as melhores compondo sua lista Global 2000.

8A tabela das 10 melhores universidades brasileiras de acordo com os quatro rankings (Arwu 2008 e 2024, CWUR e THE) mostra que todas estão localizadas no Sudeste e no Sul: quatro no estado de São Paulo, duas no Rio de Janeiro e no Rio Grande do Sul, e uma em Minas Gerais e Santa Catarina. Apenas uma universidade, a Universidade de São Paulo - USP, está entre as 200 melhores do mundo.

Quadro 1 As dez primeiras universidades brasileiras nos quatro rankings

- Universidade THE 2024 CWUR 2024 Arwu2024 Arwu 2008
- Universidade de São Paulo -USP 201–250 103 101-150 101-151
- Universidade de Campinas - Unicamp 351–400 346 401-500 201-302
- Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul - UFRGS 601–800 461 401-500 402-503
- Universidade Estadual Paulista - Unesp 601–800 419 401-500 402-503
- Universidade Federal de Rio de Janeiro - UFRJ 601–800 361 501-600 303-401
- Universidade Federal de São Paulo - UNIFESP 801–1000 589 701-800
- Universidade Federal de Minas Gerais - UFMG 801–1000 500 501-600 303-401
- Universidade Federal de Santa Catarina - UFSC 801–1000 719 701-800
- Pontifícia Universidade Católica de Rio de Janeiro (PUC-Rio) 801–1000 1610
- Pontifícia Universidade Católica do Rio Grande do Sul (PUCRS) 1001–1200 1504

9A Figura 2 plota todas as universidades que aparecem em pelo menos um dos rankings e mostra que seu número aumentou entre o Arwu 2008 e o Arwu 2024, com a inclusão de mais universidades no Sudeste-Sud e algumas no Nordeste e no Norte. A lista de classificação da CWRU inclui mais universidades nessas regiões e THE ainda mais, com alguns casos (quadrados azuis) em que é a única a incluí-las: isso se explica pelo fato de levar em conta critérios que as outras classificações ignoram. Essa particularidade justifica que se preste mais atenção a esse ranking.

Figura 2 As universidades brasileiras em quatro rankings mundiais

[![Figura 2 As universidades brasileiras em quatro rankings mundiais](https://journals.openedition.org/confins/docannexe/image/58999/img-2-small480.jpg)](https://journals.openedition.org/confins/docannexe/image/58999/img-2-small580.jpg)

## [Critères et typologie du *THE World University Ranking*](https://journals.openedition.org/confins/58999#tocfrom1n3)

10O *THE World University Ranking* classifica as universidades em termos de suas missões essenciais: *Teaching* (ambiente de aprendizagem), *Research environment* (volume, orçamentos e reputação), *Research quality* (resultados da pesquisa), *Industry* (relações com empresas e transferência de conhecimento) e *International outlook* (abertura internacional em funcionários, alunos e pesquisa). Há também uma série de classificações regionais e temáticas: universidades árabes, asiáticas, latino-americanas, “reputação mundial” e universidades jovens. O *Impact Ranking*, criado em 2019, avalia as universidades em relação aos Objetivos de Desenvolvimento Sustentável (ODDs) das Nações Unidas.

11A Tabela 2 foi construída atribuindo-se uma pontuação de 100 para cada critério à mais bem classificada das dez, e uma pontuação proporcional à sua pontuação THE às demais. Para os quatro primeiros critérios, a USP ficou em primeiro lugar, para relações com empresas, a Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro - UFRJ e para abertura internacional, a Pontifícia Universidade Católica do Rio de Janeiro (PUC-Rio).

Quadro Pontuações das dez melhores universidades brasileiras no THE World University Ranking

| Universidade | *Overall* | *Teaching* | *Research environment* | *Research quality* | *Industry* | *International outlook* |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Universidade de São Paulo -USP | 100 | 100 | 100 | 100 | 84 | 98 |
| Universidade de Campinas - Unicamp | 88 | 84 | 75 | 94 | 81 | 94 |
| Universidade Estadual Paulista - Unesp | 66 | 69 | 55 | 66 | 50 | 89 |
| Universidade Federal de Rio de Janeiro - UFRJ | 66 | 70 | 59 | 64 | 100 | 83 |
| Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul - UFRGS | 66 | 61 | 37 | 94 | 65 | 79 |
| Pontifícia Universidade Católica de Rio de Janeiro (PUC-Rio) | 58 | 56 | 50 | 65 | 78 | 100 |
| Universidade Federal de Santa Catarina - UFSC | 58 | 54 | 36 | 73 | 79 | 82 |
| Universidade Federal de São Paulo - UNIFESP | 58 | 56 | 37 | 84 | 58 | 81 |
| Universidade Federal de Minas Gerais - UFMG | 58 | 67 | 38 | 76 | 63 | 77 |
| Pontifícia Universidade Católica do Rio Grande do Sul (PUCRS) | 51 | 55 | 28 | 74 | 48 | 81 |

12Analisando os critérios nos quais o *THE World University Rankings* se baseia, pode-se esboçar uma explicação da situação relativa das universidades brasileiras.

13A Figura 3, baseada em uma classificação hierárquica ascendente (CAH) que agrupa os objetos observados de acordo com seu desvio do perfil geral, divide as universidades presentes nas quatro classificações em cinco classes:

- - A primeira (em vermelho) agrupa as que estão bem acima da média (barras horizontais à direita) para os cinco critérios;

- - A segunda (em laranja) as que estão um pouco acima da média (barras horizontais à direita) para os cinco critérios;

- - A terceira (em verde) as que estão acima da média para o relacionamento com as empresas;

- - A quarta (em azul claro) aquelas que estão abaixo da média (barras horizontais à esquerda) para todos os cinco critérios;

- - A quinta (em azul escuro) aquelas que estão bem abaixo da média (barras horizontais à esquerda) para todos os cinco critérios.

Figura 3 Tipologia em função dos critérios do THE World University Rankings

[![Figura 3 Tipologia em função dos critérios do THE World University Rankings](https://journals.openedition.org/confins/docannexe/image/58999/img-3-small480.jpg)](https://journals.openedition.org/confins/docannexe/image/58999/img-3-small580.jpg)

| 9 | **The Substance** | Coralie Fargeat | ❌ Não (Paris, França — Europa) |
| 10 | **Wicked** | Jon M. Chu (+ Irene Southwick) | ✅ Sim (Palo Alto, Califórnia, EUA) |

## Resposta

Contam com **pelo menos um diretor nascido fora da Europa** os seguintes 6 filmes:

1. **Anora** — dirigido por **Sean Baker** (nascido nos EUA)
2. **The Brutalist** — dirigido por **Brady Corbet** (nascido nos EUA)
3. **A Complete Unknown** — dirigido por **James Mangold** (nascido nos EUA)
4. **Dune: Part Two** — dirigido por **Denis Villeneuve** (nascido no Canadá)
5. **I'm Still Here** — dirigido por **Walter Salles** (nascido no Brasil)
6. **Wicked** — dirigido por **Jon M. Chu** (nascido nos EUA; coprodutor com Irene Southwick, também americana)

Os outros 4 filmes têm todos os seus diretores europeus: **Conclave** (Edward Berger, nascido na Alemanha), **Emilia Pérez** (Jacques Audiard, francês), **Nickel Boys** (RaMell Ross, nascido em Frankfurt, Alemanha) e **The Substance** (Coralie Fargeat, francesa).

The **97th Academy Awards** ceremony, presented by the [Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_of_Motion_Picture_Arts_and_Sciences "Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences") (AMPAS), took place on March 2, 2025, at the [Dolby Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolby_Theatre "Dolby Theatre") in [Hollywood, Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood,_Los_Angeles "Hollywood, Los Angeles"). During the gala, the AMPAS presented [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards") (commonly referred to as Oscars) in 23 categories honoring [films released in 2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_in_film "2024 in film"). The ceremony, televised in the United States by [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company "American Broadcasting Company") and streamed on [Hulu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hulu "Hulu"), was produced by Raj Kapoor and Katy Mullan, and was directed by [Hamish Hamilton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamish_Hamilton_(director) "Hamish Hamilton (director)").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-Hulu-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-Production_Team-6) Comedian [Conan O'Brien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_O'Brien "Conan O'Brien") hosted the show for the first time.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-Conan-7)

In related events, the Academy held its 15th [Governors Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governors_Awards "Governors Awards") ceremony at the Ray Dolby Ballroom of the [Ovation Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ovation_Hollywood "Ovation Hollywood") complex in Hollywood, on November 17, 2024.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-Governors_Awards-8) The [Academy Scientific and Technical Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Scientific_and_Technical_Award "Academy Scientific and Technical Award") were presented by host [Diego Luna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diego_Luna "Diego Luna") on April 29, 2025, in a ceremony at the [Academy Museum of Motion Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Museum_of_Motion_Pictures "Academy Museum of Motion Pictures") in Los Angeles.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-9)

*[Anora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anora "Anora")* won a leading five awards, including [Best Picture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Picture "Academy Award for Best Picture").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-Winners-10) Other winners included *[The Brutalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist "The Brutalist")* with three awards; *[Dune: Part Two](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dune:_Part_Two "Dune: Part Two")*, *[Emilia Pérez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emilia_Pérez "Emilia Pérez")*, and *[Wicked](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wicked_(2024_film) "Wicked (2024 film)")* with two awards each; and *[Conclave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conclave_(film) "Conclave (film)")*, *[Flow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flow_(2024_film) "Flow (2024 film)")*, *[I'm Not a Robot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Not_a_Robot_(film) "I'm Not a Robot (film)")*, *[I'm Still Here](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film) "I'm Still Here (2024 film)")*, *[In the Shadow of the Cypress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_the_Shadow_of_the_Cypress "In the Shadow of the Cypress")*, *[No Other Land](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No_Other_Land "No Other Land")*, *[The Only Girl in the Orchestra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Only_Girl_in_the_Orchestra "The Only Girl in the Orchestra")*, *[A Real Pain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Real_Pain "A Real Pain")*, and *[The Substance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Substance "The Substance")* with one each.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-Winners-10) The telecast drew 19.69 million viewers in the United States.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-Ratings-3)

## Winners and nominees

The nominees for the 97th Academy Awards were announced on January 23, 2025, at the [Samuel Goldwyn Theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuel_Goldwyn_Theater "Samuel Goldwyn Theater") in [Beverly Hills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beverly_Hills,_California "Beverly Hills, California"), by actress [Rachel Sennott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachel_Sennott "Rachel Sennott") and actor [Bowen Yang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bowen_Yang "Bowen Yang").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-11) *[Emilia Pérez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emilia_Pérez "Emilia Pérez")* led all nominees with thirteen nominations, the most for a non-English-language film in Oscars history; *[The Brutalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist "The Brutalist")* and *[Wicked](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wicked_(2024_film) "Wicked (2024 film)")* tied for second with ten nominations each.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-12) The winners were announced during the awards ceremony on March 2.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-Winners-10)

For the first time in Oscar history, two films, *Emilia Pérez* and *[I'm Still Here](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film) "I'm Still Here (2024 film)")*, were nominated simultaneously for Best Picture and Best International Feature.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-13) *I'm Still Here* was also the first Portuguese-language film nominated for Best Picture.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-14) With his wins for producing, directing, screenwriting, and film editing *[Anora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anora "Anora")*, [Sean Baker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Baker "Sean Baker") became the second person to win four awards in one night after [Walt Disney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walt_Disney "Walt Disney") did so at the [26th ceremony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/26th_Academy_Awards "26th Academy Awards") in 1954, and the first to do so for a single film.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-15)[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-17) Best Actor winner [Adrien Brody](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adrien_Brody "Adrien Brody") gave the longest [acceptance speech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oscar_speech "Oscar speech") in Oscar history at 5 minutes and 37 seconds.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-18) Best Actress nominee [Karla Sofía Gascón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karla_Sofía_Gascón "Karla Sofía Gascón") became the [first openly transgender performer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_LGBTQ_Academy_Award_winners_and_nominees#Confirmed_individuals_2 "List of LGBTQ Academy Award winners and nominees") to be nominated for an acting category.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-19) Best Supporting Actress winner [Zoe Saldaña](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zoe_Saldaña "Zoe Saldaña") was the first [Dominican American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominican_Americans "Dominican Americans") to win an Oscar.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-20) Best Costume Design winner [Paul Tazewell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Tazewell "Paul Tazewell") became the first Black man to win that category.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-21) Best Animated Feature winner *[Flow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flow_(2024_film) "Flow (2024 film)")* was the first [independently animated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_animation "Independent animation") film to win that category and the first Latvian film to win an Oscar.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-22) Best Documentary Feature winner *[No Other Land](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No_Other_Land "No Other Land")* became the first Palestinian film to win an Oscar.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-23)
